 The Planning Commission is making every effort to follow the spirit and intent of the
Brown Act and other applicable laws regulating the conduct of public meetings in order to
maximize transparency and public access.

In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-
related modification or accommodation to participate in this meeting, please contact the
City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

If you require oral Spanish translation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office at (661) 267-
5151 at least 72 hours prior to the meeting.

Your courtesy is requested to help our meetings run smoothly. If you’ll be kind enough to
follow these simple rules, we can make the best possible use of your time and ours:

  Please refrain from public displays or outbursts, such as unsolicited applause,
  comments, cheering, foul language or obscenities.
  Any disruptive activities that substantially interfere with the ability of the Planning
  Commission to carry out its meeting will not be permitted and offenders will be
  asked to leave the meeting.
  Please turn off/mute your cell phones and mobile devices.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  8.A  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC 2022-037 (Assistant Planner
  Sam Dominguez)
  1
 Conditional Use Permit 22-002 and Site Plan Review 22-004; a request to construct
a four-story hotel totaling approximately 65,000 square feet on two vacant parcels
totaling 2.53 acres located at the southeast corner of West Avenue P-4 and Trade
Center Drive (APNs: 3003 081-066, and -067).

Chair Nemeth opened the Public Hearing on this item.

Applicant Lee Shoeman, Vice President of Construction addressed the
Commission and stated he understood and agrees with all items in the Conditional
Use Permit.

Commissioner Elize thanked the applicant for a job well done, and inquired about
how many jobs this project will bring.

Mr. Shoeman stated that they anticipate 12-15 fulltime positions and as they
become more established, they will bring on some additional part time staffing.
Staffing will consist of a General Manager, Assistant General Manager, Sales and
Revenue, House Keeping staff, Property Engineer, and evening Security.
Commissioner Elize inquired as to whether they will hire locally. Mr Shoeman
stated that they prefer to hire locally, to have staff that knows the area.

Commissioner Elize asked if they will accept temporary housing vouchers? Mr.
Shoeman stated that if the insurance covers those circumstances, they will honor
such vouchers.

Commissioner Alvarez asked if the construction will be generated from local
laborers. Mr. Shoeman stated no contracts have been written as of yet, but they
will be looking to hire local contractors.

Chair Nemeth reminded Commissioners of items within the Commissions purview
and authority on decision making recommendations and approvals.

Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing.

Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-037 approving Conditional Use Permit
  22-002 and Site Plan Review 22-004 and find that the project is
  consistent with the previously certified Environmental Impact Report
  90-1 for the Palmdale Trade and Commerce Center Specific Plan.
Moved by:  Vice Chair Henderson seconded by Commissioner Alvarez
Motion passed with five Yes votes.

Chair Nemeth stated she was happy with the choice of landscape with
consideration for drought related design.

  2
 8.B  Public Hearing and Review of Resolution No. PC 2022-038 (Assistant Planner
  Sam Dominguez)

  Tentative Tract Map 61610; a request to subdivide approximately 10 acres into 34
  lots, for the purpose of constructing 33 single-family residences and one detention
  basin located south of Palmdale Boulevard and approximately 930 feet west of 60th
  Street East (APNS: 3023-002-022, -029, -030, -031, and -032).

  Commissioner Alvarez asked whether the applicant has already submitted the
  application related to the Palmdale Water District Conceptual Water Plan as
  mentioned within Table 2 of the staff report.

  Planning Manager Taggart informed Commissioner Alvarez that this is done during
  plan check and once the map has been reviewed by the Planning Commission as
  the decision making body it is then submitted for plan check to Building and Safety,
  Planning, Engineering, Fire and Water, for concurrent review before permits are
  issued.

  Chair Nemeth opened the Public Hearing on this item.
  No comments received.
  Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-038 approving Tentative Tract Map
  61610 and find that the project is consistent with the previously
  adopted Mitigated Negative Declaration and Mitigation Monitoring
  and Reporting Program, as amended.
  Moved by:  Commissioner Alvarez seconded by Commissioner Fraga-Saenz
  Motion passed with five Yes votes.

8.C  Public Hearing Review of Resolution No. PC 2022-035 (Associate Planner Justin
  Sauder)

  A Resolution of the Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale recommending
  City Council approval of Specific Plan Amendment 21-003 and approving Site Plan
  Review 21-012; to amend the Palmdale Transit Area Specific Plan generally bound
  by Technology Drive, 10th Place East, East Avenue Q-9 and State Route 14, and
  construct a new 3,600 square foot express car wash located on the southeast
  corner of 5th Street West and East Palmdale Boulevard (APNs: 3009-006-013, -
  014, -015 and -021).

  Chair Nemeth clarified that many items in the Specific Plan Amendment are clean
  up items on behalf of the City.

  Chair Nemeth opened the Public Hearing on this item.
  3
 Applicant Mr. Vance Shannon representing Quick Quack Carwash spoke regarding
keeping of the conservation of water in mind. He stated that they use 23-25 gallons
of water per wash which is reclaimed and recycled through an on-site system.

Commissioner Alvarez inquired if the water usage is of the top tier for carwashes.
Mr. Shannon added that their practice is to conserve water by using recycled and
reclaimed water.

Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing.

Vice Chair Henderson asked if the two items can be separated and have a different
resolution for each.

Planning Manager Taggart stated it is at the leisure of the Planning Commission to
decide to make the recommendation for the project as a whole or separate it out.

Vice Chair Henderson would like to take action on the cleanup items proposed by
the City and not related to the carwash project. The project would then require an
amendment to the Specific Plan related to transit, which currently does not allow
for car washes. He stated that his preference would be to push this project off from
Palmdale Boulevard to maintain what is written in the Specific Plan. He stated that
the architectural elevations of the project seem to not be consistent with, or to the
high quality of, some of the other versions of this particular carwash as constructed
in other locations.

Vice Chair Henderson would like to recommend that the amendment cleanup for
the Specific Plan and approval for the construction of a carwash be reviewed
separately.

Chair Nemeth asked if two separate Resolutions for City Council would be needed;
one recommending items in the Specific Plan not related to the carwash project
and one to allow approval, of the carwash.

Chair Nemeth asked for a motion to reopen the Public Hearing.

Motion:  A request to reopen the Public Hearing.
Moved by:  Commissioner Alvarez seconded by Commissioner Elize

Mr. Shannon addressed the question related to the architectural elevations and
front view of the project and stated his ability to modify some of the articulation and
character to the building and indicated that the desert scape landscape will create
a buffer from Palmdale Boulevard to further beautify the street view. He stressed
that they are a first class operation.

  4
   Commissioner Fraga-Saenz asked about the height of the building. Mr. Shannon
  answered that it is 29 feet and is for design screening purposes only.

  Planning Manager Taggart suggested that should it be desired, a motion could be
  made to recommend the items be separated in two actions to allow discussion of
  the cleanup items on the Specific Plan and then discuss the carwash items. The
  amendment would include modifying the boundary of the carwash site to eliminate
  the current split zoning.

  Chair Nemeth closed the Public Hearing.

  Assistant City Attorney Bettenhausen advised the Commissioners that staff can
  simplify and focus on the top two bullet points on page three of the staff report and
  separate the remaining bullet points for cleanup items not specific to the carwash
  project, which can be presented separately for City Council consideration and
  make the motion to approve excluding the first two bullet points should this be the
  desire of the Planning Commission.

  Motion:  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-035, recommending City Council
  approval of Specific Plan Amendment 21-003, approving Site Plan
  Review 21-012 subject to approval of SPA 21-003 by City Council, find
  that SPA 21-003 is consistent with the previously approved
  environmental documents and that SPR 21-012 is Categorically
  Exempt from environmental review, as amended by the memorandum
  provided.

  Moved by:  Chair Nemeth seconded by Commissioner Alvarez
  Motion passed with four Yes votes and one No vote by Commissioner Henderson

 9.  STAFF COMMUNICATIONS

10.  PLANNING COMMISSION COMMUNICATION

  Chair Nemeth would like to suggest that future proposed wireless telecommunications
  facilities be located on top of tall buildings, such as a hotel. Recent approval of taller

  Chair Nemeth also announced the AV Wall Mobile Memorial wall will be on 24 hour
  display from November 9th to November 13th at the Palmdale Amphitheater. The Veterans
  Day ceremony will take place on November 11th at 11:00 a.m.

  Commissioner Fraga-Saenz announced that the City hosted the Kaleidoscope event and
  had a great turnout this past weekend. Overall, feedback from the community was positive
  and she looks forward to continuing to spread the work about the event in the coming
  year.

PLANNER:  Sam Dominguez, Assistant Planner

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the Planning Commission adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-042
approving Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 22-010 and find that the project is Categorically
Exempt from environmental review.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to establish a Type 47 (beer, wine and distilled spirits)
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license to sell beer, wine and distilled
spirits within an existing 6,600 square foot restaurant located at 1205 West Rancho Vista
Boulevard. The restaurant is not proposing a dance floor or live entertainment.
Furthermore, the project does not include any expansion or exterior modification to the
existing building or associated parking area.

The on-site sale and consumption of alcohol is proposed to be incidental to the primary
restaurant operation. The alcoholic beverage component will utilize approximately
192 square feet or less than 10 percent [192/6,600) x 100 = 2.9 percent] of the gross floor
area, for the sale, display, and storage of alcohol as depicted in Figure 3. All alcohol will
be stored in a secured location within a storage room and behind the bar for on-site
consumption only.

The bona fide restaurant is permitted within the RC (Regional Commercial) General Plan
land use designation and the C-4 (Commercial Center) zone and incidental alcohol sales
are allowable subject to approval of a CUP application, as specified within Palmdale
Municipal Code (PMC) Sections 17.76.010 and 17.92.070.

BACKGROUND

The subject site was originally approved by a Hearing Officer on January 26, 2005,
through Site Plan Review (SPR) 9-04-1, which allowed for the construction of an
approximately 6,600 square foot building for use as a restaurant (Famous Dave’s). Since
then, the previous restaurant has discontinued operations and a new restaurant (Pier 88)
occupied the existing building in October 2022. The City of Palmdale has received one
application for a modification to the building. Minor Modification (MM) 22-055 was
approved on October 25, 2022, for the addition of decorative wooden bollards to the porch
in the front of the existing building.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive update to the General
Plan, the land use designation of this site will remain RC (Regional Commercial). The
approved project is consistent with the intent of the RC designation; however, as a
complete application was submitted prior to the October 22, 2022, effective date of
Palmdale 2045, this project will be evaluated using the 1993 General Plan.

SPECIAL FINDINGS FOR ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE ESTABLISHMENTS

In addition to the standard CUP findings required within PMC Section 17.22.050, the
Planning Commission must also find that the proposed use is consistent with the purpose
of PMC Section 17.92.070. That section provides:

  “It is the purpose of these regulations to establish specific standards for alcoholic
  beverage establishments to ensure that such businesses are appropriately located

Items that the Planning Commission may consider in making this finding include Over
Intensification, High Crime Area, Surrounding Area, and Hours of Operation. These
factors are detailed below.

Over Intensification

PMC Section 17.92.070 provides two methods to determine Over Intensification:
Population Density Method and Retail Density Method; both are discussed below.

Population Density Method

  Over Intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments shall occur
  where the ratio of the resident population to the permitted On-Sale Alcoholic
  Beverage Establishments (as defined by the California Department of Alcoholic
  Beverage Control) within the census tract or census division exceeds the ratio of
  population to On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments for the City.

The Population Density Method, as shown in Table 6, reveals that there is an over
intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments as defined in PMC Section
17.92.070.

High Crime Area

A high crime area is defined by PMC Section 17.16.080, as an area having a crime rate
of 120 percent or more of the average of the reporting districts within the City. According
to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, there are 33 Crime Reporting Districts
(CRD) within the City of Palmdale, with a total of 7,502 Part I and Part II Crimes reported
for the year 2021. The average number of combined Part I and Part II Crime offenses for
the reporting period, for all 33 districts, was 227 (7,502 Part I and Part II Crimes/ 33 CRD),
and 20 percent greater than that average is 272 (227 x 1.20). The project is within CRD
2618 (Figure 6), which had a total of 185 Part I and Part II offenses, according to data
provided by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. Therefore, the proposed use
is within a crime reporting area that exhibits a crime rate that is 82 percent
[(185 / 227) x 100] of the Citywide average. As such, the project site is within an area
that exhibits a crime rate that is 82 percent higher compared to all crime reporting districts
across the City and therefore the project is not considered to be in a high crime area.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided the most current location and
date information for Part I and Part II crimes reported for 2021. As shown on the 2021
Part I and Part II Crimes in CRD 2618 map (Figure 6), all 185 crimes are represented
within a single marker for the reporting district.

Calls for Service

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided a summary of service calls and
crime history for the project site between October 12, 2021, to October 12, 2022, during
a time period in which the existing building was vacant. The report indicates there has
been only one call for service. The call was for ‘suspicious circumstances-open door or
window’ where a concerned pedestrian called the Sheriff’s Department on suspicion of
trespassing on private property. Upon arrival of deputies to the site, a construction worker
was discovered doing permitted work under Building Permit No. B21-1623 for fire damage
repair and interior tenant improvements inside of the location.

After review of past service calls within CRD 2618, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department has not indicated any opposition to the approval of this CUP. In addition, as
specified within the draft Conditions of Approval, if the proposed business generates an
increase in the number of calls for service, the Sheriff’s Department may request
subsequent review of the CUP by the Planning Commission.

Surrounding Area

As specified within PMC Section 17.92.070.D, certain separations from alcohol uses to
sensitive uses are required, which are intended to ensure that such businesses are
located in a manner that avoids significant threats to public peace, health, safety, and
welfare. However, alcoholic beverage establishments within the C-4 zone are not subject
to the location standards specified within the PMC. There are residences to the northeast
of the site; however, there is a vacant field that separates the restaurant from the
residences that will act as buffer for any threats to public peace, health, safety, and
welfare. All activities occur inside the restaurant within the hours of operation, the bar is
incidental to the restaurant, and there will be no nightclub. The remainder of the uses in
the vicinity consist of commercial retail businesses, restaurants, service uses, and other
supportive uses. In addition, there is a church and a school to the north across Avenue
O-8; however, State Route 14 runs in between the two parcels and therefore creates a
buffer and helps further reduce any potential negative impact. As such, the location is
appropriate for this type of use.

Operations

The restaurant operates from 10:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily. The applicant will be
required to comply with all Conditions of Approval, restrictions of the ABC license, ABC
regulations, and reapply for a new ABC license should the use of the premises qualify for

a different license type. The sale, storage, and display of beer, wine and distilled spirits
will utilize less than 10 percent of the floor area and is incidental to the primary restaurant
use. Also, Conditions of Approval have been included within draft Resolution No. PC-
2022-042 prohibiting the sale of alcohol for off-site consumption. Therefore, the proposed
project is not expected to adversely affect nearby property.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is categorically exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) Guidelines review pursuant to Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines, which
exempts licensing of existing uses with negligible expansion of the use. The proposed
project will allow for a Type 47 ABC license for beer, wine, and distilled spirits sales for
on-site consumption within a bona fide restaurant, which is expected to be a negligible
expansion of the existing restaurant use.

OPTIONS

The Planning Commission has the following options:

1.  Adopt Resolution No. PC-2022-042 approving CUP 22-010 and find that the
  project is Categorically Exempt from environmental review.

2.  Continue the project and direct staff to return with additional information.

3.  Deny the project.

Option 1 is recommended.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The proposed project is a request for a 10-year time extension for the continued operation
of an existing major wireless telecommunications facility located at 4618 East Avenue S.
The facility was previously approved as a 55-foot-high monopole with a 340 square foot
equipment enclosure.

BACKGROUND

On May 3, 2001, the Planning Commission approved CUP 00-09 (Resolution No.
PC-2001-024), which allowed for the construction of a 55-foot-high major wireless
telecommunications facility, with two wireless carriers, and 178 square foot equipment
enclosure.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Section 17.95.040.E.1 and the Conditions
of Approval for CUP 00-09, wireless facilities expire in 10 years, unless a time extension
application for the CUP is approved. Because a time extension application was not
received prior to expiration of the major wireless telecommunications facility, the
entitlement expired, and a new CUP was required for the continued operation of the
facility. On June 14, 2012, the Planning Commission approved CUP 11-025 (Resolution
No. PC-2012-012), which allowed for a 10-foot increase in the height of the monopole to
accommodate a third wireless carrier; however, the ten-foot height increase was not
constructed. The facility was subsequently modified through Minor Modifications (MM)
12-039, 15-013, and 17-025, and 22-003. The second carrier antennas are currently not
flush mounted, which is inconsistent with the Conditions of Approval for CUP 11-025 and
staff has been unable to locate approval of this modification. As such, a Condition of
Approval will be included within the draft Resolution to require future modifications to
comply with the antenna placement requirements.

The subject application was initially submitted on May 12, 2022, prior to the
June 26, 2022, expiration date, and was deemed incomplete. After resolution of
completeness items, the application was deemed complete and scheduled for the
November 10, 2022, Planning Commission meeting.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive General Plan Update,
the land use designation of this site has been changed to Regional Commercial (RC).
The project is consistent with the intent of the RC designation; however, as a complete
or substantially complete application was submitted prior to the October 22, 2022,
effective date of Palmdale 2045, this project will be evaluated based on the previous land
use designation and zoning standards.

Design

The existing major wireless telecommunications facility is designed as a gray monopole,
supports two wireless carriers, and is located within a neutral-colored enclosure
constructed of concrete masonry units. Condition of Approval No. 17, within CUP 11-025
requires that “the monopole shall consist of a flush mounted panel antenna design as
shown and specified in the site plan and elevation plans date stamped March 5, 2012”
and “antennas shall be flush mounted to the pole and shall not extend beyond the existing
panel antennas.” The existing facility does not currently meet these requirements
because the second wireless carrier antennas are not flush mounted and extend beyond
the approved antenna placement; however, with the incorporation of a Condition of
Approval to require any physical modifications by the second wireless carrier to redesign
the antenna array to comply with antenna placement requirements, the existing major
wireless telecommunications facility will comply with the design standards found within
PMC Section 17.95.040.D.5. In addition, no advertising, signs, or graphics are present
on the existing structures.

A.  RECITALS

  1.  SBA 2012 TC Assets, LLC has filed an application requesting the approval
  of Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 11-025 Time Extension (TE), for a 10-year
  time extension for a previously approved major wireless
  telecommunications facility, described herein (hereinafter referred to as
  “Application”).

  2.  The Application applies to a major wireless telecommunications facility
  located at 4618 East Avenue S indicated on the Los Angeles County
  Assessor’s roll as Accessor’s Parcel Number 3052-001-040, legally
  described on Exhibit I hereto and shown on the map attached hereto as
  Exhibit II.

  3.  On November 10, 2022, the Planning Commission of the City of Palmdale
  conducted a duly noticed public hearing on the Application and concluded
  said hearing on that date.

  4.  All legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have occurred.

B.  RESOLUTION

  NOW THEREFORE, it is hereby found, determined, and resolved by the Planning
  Commission of the City of Palmdale, as follows:

  1.  The Planning Commission hereby specifically finds that all of the facts set
  forth in the Recitals, Part A of this Resolution, are true and correct.

  2.  The Planning Commission hereby finds as follows with respect to the
  environmental document:

  (a)  Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, an Initial Study was prepared for the project in
  conjunction with the original approval and on June 14, 2012, the
  Planning Commission adopted a MND finding that, with the
  incorporation of mitigation measures, the project would not have a
  significant impact on the environment. Staff has reviewed the MND
  to determine whether the project triggered any of the conditions
  described in Sections 15162, 15163, and 15164 of the CEQA
  Guidelines and determined that additional documentation is not
  required for the project because CUP 11-025 TE does not propose
  any significant revisions to the project, there are no changes in
  circumstances and there is no new information of substantial
  importance that will involve new significant environmental effects or
  increase the severity of previously identified significant effects. The
  proposed project is a request to continue the operation of an existing
  major wireless telecommunications facility and does not include any
  significant alterations to the major wireless telecommunications
  facility as approved through CUP 11-025. Furthermore, an RF report
  has been submitted and indicated that the project will continue to be
  compliant with FCC rules and regulations, as described in Bulletin
  65.

  (b)  The custodian of records for the environmental document, and all
  other materials which constitute the record of proceedings upon
  which the Planning Commission’s decision is based, is the Planning
  Manager of the City of Palmdale. These documents are available for
  public review in the Planning Division of the City of Palmdale located
  at 38250 Sierra Highway, Palmdale, California 93550, telephone
  (661) 267-5200.

  3.  Based upon substantial evidence presented to this Commission during the
  above-referenced November 10, 2022, public hearing, including public
  testimony, and written and oral staff report, this Commission specifically
  finds as follows:

  (a)  The proposed facility has been designed and located in compliance
  with all applicable provisions of the Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC),
  including Section 17.95.050.

  The Application, as conditioned, is consistent with the goals, policies,
  and objectives of the General Plan, as well as PMC Section
  17.95.040 as shown in Exhibits III and IV attached hereto. The
  continued  operation  of  the  existing  major  wireless
  telecommunications facility provides continued telecommunication
  capabilities in the City. In addition, the enclosure consists of earth
  tone colors to avoid potentially offensive aesthetic impacts and
  ensure compliance with the PMC.

  (b)  The proposed location for the facility is reasonable when considering
  both (1) the Federal mandate to not regulate personal wireless
  service facilities in a manner that would “prohibit or have the effect
  of prohibiting the provision of personal wireless services”; and (2) the
  City’s legitimate related policy objectives relating to the location of
  wireless facilities.

  The Application is for the continued use of an existing major wireless
  telecommunications facility. This Application does not include any
  significant alterations to the major wireless telecommunications
  facility as approved through CUP 11-025, which has previously been
  found to be consistent with all provisions of the PMC in regard to
  location, height, aesthetic, and safety standards as demonstrated in
  Exhibit IV. In addition, a Condition of Approval has been included to
  require the collocated wireless carrier to bring the existing antenna
  array, which was installed in a manner inconsistent with the
  Conditions of Approval for CUP 11-025, into compliance in
  conjunction with the next submitted modification application in order
  to minimize the aesthetic impact of the facility to the neighboring
  commercial uses.

  (c)  The proposed facility is substantially compatible with existing or
  planned developments and uses in the same general area and would
  not be substantially detrimental to existing or planned developments
  or uses within the general area.

  The existing major wireless telecommunications facility provides
  wireless service to cell users within the vicinity of the tower and is
  compatible with the existing commercial use of the area. The height
  and location of the facility and equipment enclosure have not been
  modified since original approval; however, the antenna array is
  currently not in compliance with the Conditions of Approval as
  specified within CUP 11-025 (Resolution No. PC-2012-012). As
  such, a Condition of Approval has been included to require the
  collocated wireless carrier to bring the existing antenna array, which
  was installed in a manner inconsistent with the Conditions of
  Approval for CUP 11-025, into compliance in conjunction with the
  next submitted modification application in order to minimize the
  aesthetic impact of the facility to the neighboring commercial uses.

  (d)  The proposed facility will not be materially detrimental to the health,
  safety, and general welfare of the public (excluding any
  environmental effects of radio frequency emissions to the extent that
  such facilities comply with the Federal Communication
  Commission’s regulations concerning such emissions).

  The Application proposes no changes to the existing major wireless
  telecommunications facility. The continued operation of the facility,
  as conditioned, will not have a substantial adverse effect on the
  environment or abutting property, because the provided radio
  frequency (RF) emission survey indicates the maximum levels of RF
  emissions exposure do not exceed all applicable Federal
  Communications Commission limits of exposure.

  (e)  All antennas, poles, equipment, and other structures erected to
  support antennas are visually compatible with their surroundings.

  The major wireless telecommunications facility consists of a 55-foot-
  high monopole. The height and location of the facility and equipment

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicants are requesting a two-year time extension for a previously approved 21-
acre commercial and residential development located at the northwest corner of
Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West. The project consists of a 308-unit
apartment complex, 36-unit townhome development, and approximately 47,000 square
feet of retail/commercial development on a vacant site. The commercial complex is
located at the northwest corner of 15th Street West and Rancho Vista Boulevard within
the southern portion of the site. The apartment complex is located on the northern portion
of the site and the townhomes are located on the western portion of the site. No changes
to the site are proposed as part of this time extension application. LaTerra Development
is the applicant for the residential portion of the site and Sage Investco is the applicant
for the commercial portion.

BACKGROUND

The project was originally approved by the Planning Commission on July 11, 2019,
though Resolution No. PC-2019-027 for Planned Development (PD) 19-001,
Tentative Tract Map (TTM) 82636, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) 19-002, and
SPR 19-003 for the development of a mixed-use project. On August 6, 2019, the City
Council approved General Plan Amendment (GPA) 19-001 and Zone Change (ZC)
19-001 through Resolution No. CC-2019-068 in conjunction with the above approvals.
Following approval of the development, applications were approved by the Planning
Commission on May 13, 2021, through Resolution No. PC-2021-012 to phase the
subdivision of the site through TTM 82636 Major Modification No. 1. In addition, the
commercial portion of the project has been modified through Minor Modifications 19-075,
21-036, and 21-066, and the residential portion through Minor Modification 22-018.

GPA 19-001 and ZC 19-001 approved changes to the land use designation and zone to
accommodate the residential components of the project, PD 19-001 allowed flexibility of
development standards, TTM 82636 and TTM 82636 Major Modification approved the
subdivision and phasing of lots, and CUP 19-002 allowed the sale of beer and wine
(Alcoholic Beverage Control License Type 20 – Off-sale Beer and Wine) within a
proposed grocery store in the commercial component of the site.

PD 19-001 was approved for a period of five years, establishing an expiration date of
July 23, 2024. On March 2, 2022, the City Council adopted Urgency Ordinance U-1582
amending Palmdale Municipal Code Section 16.40.120 to increase the initial term of
tentative maps by one year for housing projects that were in effect on March 1, 2022, and
 Staff Report to the Planning Commission

that will expire before December 31, 2022. As such, the expiration date of TTM 82636
was extended until July 23, 2023, and CUP 19-002 and SPR 19-003 expired on
July 23, 2022.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive General Plan Update,
the land use designation of this site has been changed to Mixed Use 2 (MU2). The
approved project is consistent with the intent of the MU2 designation; however, as a
complete, or substantially complete application was submitted prior to the
October 22, 2022, effective date of Palmdale 2045, this project will be evaluated based
on the previous land use designation, the planned development document, and any
applicable standards.

The proposed time extension application was submitted on June 8, 2022, and was
deemed incomplete. After resolution of completeness items, the application was deemed
complete on September 12, 2022, and scheduled for the November 10, 2022, Planning
Commission meeting.

The project site is currently fenced off as development activity is on-going. The
commercial and residential components of the project are both in the process of procuring
grading and building permits; however, above ground construction has not yet
commenced.

Access/Circulation

Vehicular access to the site will be provided from four new driveways: one on
Rancho Vista Boulevard and three on 15th Street West. Right-turn lanes will be provided
at the north and south driveways on 15th Street West and the driveway on
Rancho Vista Boulevard. Vehicles exiting the site will be able to make right and left
turning movements out of the 15th Street West driveways and only right turning
movements out of the Rancho Vista Boulevard driveway.

In addition, two emergency access points are provided onto 15th Street West from the
apartment portion of the site for use by Los Angeles County Fire Department apparatus
only. These access drives will be clearly marked and are not intended to be open for
public vehicular ingress or egress to the site. No changes are proposed as part of this
time extension.

Pedestrian access will be provided into the site through the installation of sidewalks
adjacent to the project along all street frontages. In addition, pedestrian access, shaded
through the use of pergolas and landscaping, will be provided throughout the site and
include connections from the residential portions of the site to the commercial portion of
the site, as well as to surrounding development.

Elevations

The PD establishes design standards to ensure a cohesive design and compatible
architecture for both the residential and commercial portions of the site. The colors and
materials for the approved project have been modified through minor modifications;
however, no additional changes are proposed as part of this application.

2.  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

A.  Project Location

  6
   The Proposed Project site is a vacant parcel located at the northwest corner of
  Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale. West
  Avenue O-12 (a private drive) is located to the north of the Proposed Project site,
  15th Street West is to the east, and Rancho Vista Boulevard is to the south. An
  existing residential tract borders the site on the west.

B.  Project Setting

  The General Plan land use designation of the Proposed Project site is CC
  (Community Commercial) and the property is zoned C-3 (General Commercial).
  Land uses surrounding the Proposed Project site include Regional Commercial
  (RC) to the east, and Single Family Residential (SFR-3) to the south and west.
  Zoning surrounding the Proposed Project site includes C-4 (Commercial Center)
  to the east, and Single Family Residential (R-1-7,000) to the south and west
  which designates a minimum lot size of 7,000 square feet. The properties to the
  north of the site are within Los Angeles County jurisdiction and according to the
  Los Angeles Planning and Zoning for Unincorporated Los Angeles County, the
  area north of the site is zoned for Heavy Agricultural (A-2).

  Antelope Valley Mall is located east of 15th Street West and the Proposed
  Project site. It consists of a large central retail center, with an entrance and
  parking lot adjacent to 15th Street West. Single-family homes are located south
  of the Proposed Project site across Rancho Vista Boulevard and immediately
  west of the Proposed Project site along Dover Drive. A block wall separates the
  houses along Dover Drive from the Proposed Project site. Homes south of
  Rancho Vista Boulevard also have a block wall that separates the homes from
  the sidewalk along the street. North of the Proposed Project are fenced
  residential properties. West Avenue O-12, along 15th Street West, is a private
  unpaved roadway.

C.  Project Components

  The Applicant proposes the construction of a mixed-use development including
  multi-family residential and commercial facilities on the vacant 20.55-acre
  property. The Proposed Project consists of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-
  unit townhome development, and 43,200 square feet of retail/commercial
  development. The Proposed Project components are summarized below:

mixed-use site. The current land use and zoning designation does not include a
residential component. The zone change and General Plan amendment would
allow residential facilities to be included on the site.

Access

  8
   Access to the apartments will be provided through a main gated entrance along
  15th Street West. There is also an Emergency Vehicle access point towards the
  north side of the complex on 15th Street East. The Apartments also have a
  second gated access into the complex from the commercial center. The
  Commercial Center will have three entrances, a main access and a service lane
  entrance on 15th Street West and a main access on Ranch Vista Boulevard. The
  Townhomes will have gated access from the commercial center drive from
  Rancho Vista Boulevard and access from the apartment complex.

  Project Construction

  Construction for the Proposed Project is anticipated to begin in Fall 2019. The
  proposed construction will occur in a single phase with the following estimated
  duration: apartments construction for 18 months, townhomes construction for 12
  months, and retail construction for 10 months, not including interior
  improvements. The commercial center is anticipated to be operational by late
  Spring 2020. The Proposed Project area will be graded prior to building
  construction. Construction activities are scheduled to occur Monday through
  Friday. Per the City of Palmdale Municipal Code, building construction hours will
  be restricted between the hours of 8:00 PM to 6:30 AM. Equipment to be used
  onsite includes excavators, earthmovers, frontend loaders, backhoes,
  compactors, cement mixers, water trucks, cranes, forklifts, and other typical
  construction equipment. Staging areas for the Proposed Project will be located
  onsite.

Each of the responses in the following environmental checklist considers the whole
action involved, including project-level, cumulative, on-site, off-site, indirect,
construction, and operational impacts. A brief explanation is provided for all answers
and supported by the information sources cited.

  1. A “No Impact” answer is adequately supported if the referenced information

  2. A “Less Than Significant Impact” applies when the proposed project would
  not result in a substantial and adverse change in the environment. This
  impact level does not require mitigation measures.

  3. A “Less Than Significant Impact With Mitigation Incorporated” applies when
  the proposed project would not result in a substantial and adverse change in
  the environment after additional mitigation measures are applied.

  4. “Potentially Significant Impact” is appropriate if there is substantial evidence
  that an effect is significant. If there are one or more “Potentially Significant”
  entries when the determination is made, an EIR is required.

Project Impacts and Mitigation Measures

a)  Less Than Significant Impact. The City of Palmdale General Plan (City of
  Palmdale 1993) identifies open space, landscaped corridors, and viewsheds of
  the surrounding Angeles National Forest as providing visual enhancement and
  pleasure. Specific areas identified as containing aesthetically significant
  resources worthy of preserving include: Lamont Oddett Vista Point, Godde Hills
  Road, Bouquet Canyon Road, and Juniper Hills Road. The Proposed Project site
  is not in the vicinity of these identified aesthetic resources. Scenic vistas, or
  scenic viewsheds or backdrops as identified in the General Plan, refer to the
  significant ridgelines of the San Gabriel mountains, the Sierra Pelona range, and
  the Ritter and Portal Ridges that form the City’s skyline views. The Proposed
  Project is located within an urban and built-out environment and is not in the
  vicinity of any landscaped corridors or open space. Viewsheds of Angeles
  National Forest or the General Plan’s scenic viewsheds would not be significantly
  altered due to implementation of the Proposed Project. There are no parks or
  trails located nearby the Proposed Project where it would block any views of the
  ridgelines. A bus stop is located at the southern portion of the Proposed Project
  site along Rancho Vista Boulevard. However, the bus stop is facing south, and
  users’ views of the ridgelines will not be obstructed. Views of the mountains may
  be temporarily blocked while driving along Rancho Vista Boulevard but the
  intermittent blockage of views would not constitute a significant impact.
  Therefore, implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than
  significant impact associated with scenic vistas.

  18
 b)  No Impact. Currently, no officially designated or eligible state scenic highways
  are near the Proposed Project site. The nearest designated or eligible state
  scenic highway is Interstate 210, approximately 25 miles southwest of the
  Proposed Project site (Caltrans 2011).

c)  Less Than Significant Impact. The General Plan land use designation of the
  Proposed Project site is CC (Community Commercial) and the site is zoned C-3
  (General Commercial). Land uses surrounding the Proposed Project site are
  within the unincorporated Los Angeles County jurisdiction areas to the north, RC
  (Regional Commercial) to the east, Single-Family Residential (SFR-3 [3.1-6
  du/ac]) to the south and west. Zoning surrounding the Proposed Project site
  include unincorporated Los Angeles County jurisdiction areas to the north, C-4
  (Commercial Center) to the east, and Single-Family Residential (R-1-7,000) to
  the south and west. The Community Commercial (CC) designation is intended for
  businesses providing retail and service uses which primarily serve the local
  market. Representative uses include restaurants, apparel stores, hardware
  stores, grocery markets, banks, offices, and similar uses. The Proposed Project
  will include a site plan review , zone change, and General Plan amendment for
  the development of a mixed-use site which would consist of residential and
  commercial uses.

  The presence of construction equipment and materials during the construction
  phase could result in the disturbance of the existing character of the site.
  Construction impacts could include fencing of the Proposed Project area,
  signage, lighting, and transporting of equipment. Once fully built, the Proposed
  Project would result in a permanent impact to the visual character of the
  Proposed Project area with the presence of the residences and commercial
  properties with the maximum height of 45 feet .

  The development of the Proposed Project will construct a live-work space by
  providing residents access to retail and commercial businesses within walking
  distance of their neighborhood. The construction of the Proposed Project would
  replace the vacant and disturbed lot and would utilize building materials that
  would complement the aesthetics of the existing residences, retail, and
  commercial buildings. Additionally, the Proposed Project would comply with
  Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Sections 17.86.010 and 17.87.050.H.2 which
  will require landscaping associated with the Proposed Project to maximize the
  aesthetic quality on site.

  While the Proposed Project would result in visual impacts during construction
  such as the presence of equipment, vehicles, and construction fencing around
  the site, these impacts would be short term in nature and limited to the
  construction phase only. In addition, the Proposed Project would include
  construction BMPs including but not limited to proper storage of equipment,
  project site maintenance and clean up, dust control measures, and limiting hours
  of construction within the hours mandated by the PMC in order to minimize any

  19
   impacts regarding the visual character of the area.

  Permanent impacts would include the presence of a new development on a
  currently vacant lot. The Proposed Project is located within an urbanized area
  and the surroundings are fully developed with residential and commercial
  buildings. The Proposed Project uses would be consistent with the General Plan
  with the approval of the proposed General Plan Amendment and the building
  height will be compatible with heights allowed within the surrounding area.
  According to PMC Section 17.16.020, primary structures are not to exceed 45
  feet for buildings in the C-3 (General Commercial) zone and R-3 (multiple-family
  residential) zone and 60 feet in the R-4 (high-density residential) zone.
  Additionally, there are no resources on site that hold scenic value. Therefore,
  implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than significant
  impact associated with visual character and scenic quality.

d)  Less Than Significant Impact. The Proposed Project will include temporary and
  permanent lighting to the Proposed Project area.

  During construction, the Proposed Project will include temporary construction
  lighting for areas requiring additional lighting such as confined spaces, and any
  digging. The Proposed Project will limit construction hours within the PMC
  requirement where construction activities are restricted between 8:00 PM to 6:30
  AM. Other additional lighting sources would come from vehicles and other large
  operating equipment. Once operational, permanent lighting sources will be from
  outdoor lighting necessary to ensure safety and vehicle lights.

  Lighting associated with the Proposed Project would be required to comply with
  PMC Section 17.86.030 which requires consistent illumination levels with the
  character and use of surrounding development; excessive illumination is not
  allowed. Additionally, exterior lighting would be required to be located and
  designed to minimize glare beyond the Proposed Project site; glare onto adjacent
  properties will be minimized by using downcast, cut-off type fixtures, as
  necessary, that are shielded and would direct the light towards specific areas
  requiring illumination. For areas that are located nearby residents, the lowest
  allowable lighting levels will be used.

  The Proposed Project also includes submittal of a Planned Development
  document, which provides specific development standards for this Project. The
  Planned Development document does not propose any changes to the lighting
  requirements as specified within PMC Section 17.86.030.  Therefore,
  implementation of the Proposed Project would result in a less than significant
  impact associated with light or glare.

Based on the client’s input on the data request form, this Proposed Project will
require 1,500 cubic yards of material export during the Site Preparation phase

dust from Project construction sites. AVAQMD Rule 403 requires that fugitive
dust from any “active operation, open storage pile or disturbed surface area” be
controlled so that no presence of dust remains visible beyond the property line.
To meet this requirement, the standard operation is watering active sites three
times per day. Although the addition of watering for dust control is listed as a
mitigation measure in CalEEMod, within the AVAQMD this is a requirement, and
is therefore included in the construction.

Operational Emissions
Operational emissions consist of area sources (i.e., re-applying architectural
coatings, consumer products, and landscaping equipment), energy use (i.e.,
electricity and natural gas), mobile sources (e.g., commuting), stationary sources
(i.e., emergency generator), solid waste disposal, and water and wastewater use
(i.e., supplying and treating water and wastewater).

For area source architectural coating operations (i.e., re-applying coatings), VOC
emissions were calculated based on the assumption that the coatings would be
compliant with the VOC content limits of the AVAQMD’s Rule 1113.

Based on client input, the residential units will not have fireplaces or woodstoves
installed. In addition, the apartment buildings may have emergency generators
installed. To quantify the potential emissions, it was assumed that a 150-
horsepower natural gas-fired emergency generator would be installed. The
emissions from the emergency generator were conservatively estimated
assuming a maximum daily usage of 24 hours per day and a maximum annual
usage of 500 hours per year.

For mobile source emissions, the number of trips were calculated using the trip
rates (weekday trip rates) that were included in the traffic study and the Saturday
and Sunday trip rates that were provided by David Evans and Associates, Inc. As
stated previously in this report, the residential emissions were modeled using
three land use types in CalEEMod. The Institute of Transportation Engineers
(ITE) Trip Generation manual, 10th Edition combines the apartments and

   condominiums/townhomes under the same Multifamily Housing land use type.
  This is why the same trip rate is used for the individual residential land use types
  in CalEEMod.

A Biological Resource Assessment and Native Vegetation Preservation Plan was
prepared for the Proposed Project by Mark Hagan, Wildlife Biologist, in February 2019
(Appendix B). The study was conducted to provide an assessment of biological
resources potentially occurring within, or utilizing the Proposed Project and also was
conducted to provide an estimated density and distribution of Joshua tree and California
juniper ecotone. A total of 12 line transects were walked on January 25, 2019 to
inventory biological resources.

Project Impacts and Mitigation Measures

a)  Less than Significant with Mitigation Incorporated.

  During the biological survey of the site, scattered litter, trash, shopping carts, and
  debris were observed within the Proposed Project area. In addition, off-highway
  vehicle tracks, dirt tracks, and a dirt road was observed. Foot and bike traffic was
  observed, including an individual riding a bike within the area during the field
  survey. A homeless encampment was observed within the study site; and

  29
 evidence of fire was observed.

The Proposed Project area was characteristic of a highly disturbed desert scrub
habitat. A total of 27 plant species were observed during the transect surveys.
California juniper was the dominant perennial species throughout the study area.
Red stemmed filaree (Erodium cicutarium) was the dominant annual species
within the study area. A total of 32 Joshua trees and 135 California juniper trees
were observed within the study area. No sensitive plant species were observed
within the study area.

A total of 17 wildlife species, or their sign were observed during the line transect
survey. No desert tortoises or their sign were observed during the field survey.
No burrowing owls or their sign were observed during the field survey. No
California ground squirrels (Citellus beecheyi) were observed on the study site.
Three inactive bird nests were observed within the study site, one in a Joshua
tree, two in silver cholla (Opuntia echinocarpa), and no nests were seen in the
California juniper trees.

The Mohave ground squirrel is a state listed threatened species; however the
Proposed Project area was not located within the geographic range of the
Mohave ground squirrel. The western limit of the geographic range of the
Mohave ground squirrel is currently thought to be Highway 14. The study area
appeared unsuitable to support Mohave ground squirrels, as human impacts on
the site are high and the site is adjacent to development on all four sides. No
mitigation for the Mohave ground squirrel is recommended.

Burrowing owls are considered a species of special concern by the California
Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW). While none were identified to be within
the Proposed Project area, the burrows of the California ground squirrel can
provide potential cover sites for burrowing owls and, as a result, may result in the
potential presence of burrowing owls.

The following mitigation measures are recommended regarding burrowing owls:

BIO-1:  A burrowing owl survey shall be accomplished within 30 days prior
  to any ground disturbing activities to ensure the absence of
  burrowing owl within the boundaries of disturbance. If the presence
  of burrowing owls is discovered, the California Department of Fish
  and Wildlife shall be consulted, and standard protocols shall be
  adhered to, prior to the occurrence of any ground disturbance.

The Proposed Project would not have a substantial adverse effect through
modification of habitats of candidate, sensitive, or special status species due to
the existing conditions of the Proposed Project area. The results of the Biological

A two-year maintenance program will be established in accordance with the
guidelines of the PMC Chapter 14.04. Joshua trees should be planted at least
ten feet apart and well-watered immediately. Joshua trees transplanted during
fall, winter, or early spring should be adequately watered once a week for two
months following transplanting. Joshua trees transplanted during late spring or
summer should be adequately watered until the end of hot weather. If sufficient
rainfall or low evaporation rates occur and the soil remains moist these watering
schedules should be reduced in frequency. Joshua trees should be planted in a
sandy, well-drained soil. Transplanting with some of the native shrubs
immediately around the Joshua tree may help in survival of individual trees.
Construction activity should not occur within twenty-five feet of transplanted

in the ground, or other means. The method of permanent marking utilized should
not harm the Joshua trees. The permanent marking should include information
that designates the date the Joshua tree was transplanted, project site the
Joshua tree came from, and point of contact name, address, and phone number.
Prior to transplanting Joshua trees, the method of marking and information
provided must be included within the Native Preservation Plan and submitted to
the City for approval.

Two years following Joshua tree transplanting, a written report must be submitted
to the City as specified by the Native Preservation Plan. This report will provide

trees surviving. Therefore, the Proposed Project will not conflict with any City

Historical Seismicity
The Palmdale area is in the seismically active southern California with at least
eight prominent major earthquakes historically affecting the area. These include
the 1812 Wrightwood, 1857 Fort Tejon, 1872 Owens Valley, 1952 Arvin‐
Tehachapi, 1971 San Fernando, 1992 Landers, 1994 Northridge, and 1999
Hector Mine earthquakes. Strong ground motions were experienced with
magnitudes ranging from approximately 6.5 to 7.9. Approximately 35 magnitude
5.5 or greater historic earthquakes have occurred within 60 miles of the
Proposed Project.

Design and construction of the new facilities would comply with all seismic-safety
development requirements, including the Title 24 standards of the current
California Building Code. Therefore, implementation of the Proposed Project
would result in a less than significant impact associated with strong seismic
ground shaking.

iii) Less Than Significant Impact.

Soil Liquefaction and Lateral Spreading
Liquefaction is the loss of soil strength from sudden shock (usually earthquake
shaking), causing the soil to become a fluid mass. Liquefaction describes a
phenomenon in which saturated soil loses shear strength and deforms as a result
of increased pore water pressure induced by strong ground shaking during an
earthquake. Dissipation of the excess pore pressures will produce volume
changes within the liquefied soil layer, which can cause settlement. Shear
strength reduction combined with inertial forces from the ground motion may also
result in lateral migration (lateral spreading). Factors known to influence
liquefaction include soil type, structure, grain size, relative density, confining
pressure, depth to groundwater, and the intensity and duration of ground
shaking. Soils most susceptible to liquefaction are saturated, loose sandy soils
and low plasticity clay and silt. In general, for the effects of liquefaction to be
manifested, groundwater levels must be within 50 feet of the ground surface and
the soils within the saturated zone must also be susceptible to liquefaction. The
project does not lie in a zone designated by California Geologic Survey for the
Ritter Ridge Quadrangle. Our exploration did not reveal a shallow groundwater
table or a perched water table. Our research of nearby water well data and
historic groundwater levels indicate both current and historic groundwater tables
are greater than 50 feet below the ground surface. Since groundwater tables are
greater than 50 feet below the existing ground surface (bgs), the estimated the

  41
   potential for liquefaction at the site is low.

  Lateral spreading (lateral migration) is caused when a loose and saturated soil
  layer is liquefied by a nearby earthquake of sufficient magnitude and a sloping
  ground, free face conditions, or sufficient building/embankment stresses exist
  near the site. Currently, these factors are not present at this site. The field and
  laboratory testing indicate that the soils within 50 feet of the surface are not
  subject to liquefaction. Therefore, lateral spreading at this site has a low potential
  (Appendix D).

  Because the Proposed Project site is not subject to liquefaction and contains low
  potential for lateral spreading, potential impacts associated with liquefaction or
  ground-failure is less than significant.

  PM) peak period turn movement counts in April 2018, provided in Exhibit C.

The Background (Cumulative) Conditions scenario evaluates impacts due to
ambient growth and traffic generated by other area projects within the study area

(Cumulative) Condition traffic volumes.

   1. PROJECT OVERVIEW

A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) was prepared in 2019 for the construction of a
mixed-use development on a vacant 20.55-acre parcel located at the northwest corner of
Rancho Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale (City). The 2019
Project, also known as the Strata West Palmdale Apartments and Strata Commons,
consisted of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-unit townhome development, and 43,200
square feet of retail/commercial development. The 2019 Project site was zoned as
General Commercial (C-3), which allows commercial shopping centers with approval of a
site plan review application. In the City’s General Plan, the 2019 Project site was
designated as Community Commercial (CC), which is intended for businesses providing
retail and service uses that serve the local market (i.e. restaurants, apparel stores,
hardware stores, grocery markets, banks, offices, and similar uses). The 2019 Project
included a conditional use permit, site plan review, tentative tract map (TTM), zone
change, and general plan amendment for the development of a mixed-use site. The 2019
Project was approved by the City Council in August 2019.

The Proposed Project site is a vacant parcel located at the northwest corner of Rancho
Vista Boulevard and 15th Street West in the City of Palmdale. West Avenue O-12 (a
private drive) is located to the north of the Proposed Project site, 15th Street West is to
the east, and Rancho Vista Boulevard is to the south. An existing residential tract borders
the site on the west. Existing conditions have not changed significantly from the previous
2019 analysis.

On September 22, 2020 the California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) accepted
the petition to list the western Joshua tree (Yucca brevifolia) as threatened or endangered
under the California Endangered Species Act (CESA). In accepting the petition, the
western Joshua tree was listed as a candidate species, defined by Section 2068 of the
Fish and Game Code, and is fully protected under CESA effective October 9, 2020 (CFGC
2020b). According to the Biological Resource Assessment and Native Vegetation
Preservation Plan prepared for the 2019 Project, a total of 32 western Joshua trees were
observed on the site (Hagan 2019). The Proposed Project must comply with both the
Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) in relation to the western Joshua trees.

Coyne Development (Applicant) proposes to transplant and remove a portion of the 32
western Joshua trees in compliance with the required permits for the approved project
and per Section 14.04 of the PMC. In addition, CDFW is a Responsible Agency under
CEQA and the Applicant must apply for an Incidental Take Permit from CDFW and pay
mitigation fees to CDFW for the take of western Joshua trees. The Proposed Project must
also comply with the PMC during the removal of western Joshua trees.

Since the approval of the 2019 Project, the following updates to the project are proposed
(Proposed Project):

  •  The proposed TTM and construction activities are proposed to occur in phases.
  •  The Proposed Project must comply with regulations for the western Joshua
   tree.

  3. SUMMARY

Article 11, Section 15162 of the CEQA Guidelines state that when an environmental
impact report (EIR) or negative declaration has been certified and adopted, no
subsequent document shall be prepared unless the lead agency determines that the
changes proposed would require major revisions to the certified environmental document,
would result in new and significant environmental effects, and/or new changes would
result in the increase in the severity of a previously identified significant effect. The
Proposed Project does not meet the criteria identified in Section 15162 of the CEQA
Guidelines based on the following:

Condition 1:

  ▪  Substantial changes in the project requires major revision to the previously
  prepared Initial Study due to the involvement of new significant environmental
  effects or substantial increase in the severity of previously identified effects;

The location of the Proposed Project site has been previously analyzed in the 2019
Project MND for the development of a 308-unit apartment complex, 36-unit townhome
development, and 43,200 square feet of retail/commercial development on the 20.55-acre
property. The site plan and development footprint of the Proposed Project would remain
the same as the site plan and development footprint previously analyzed by the 2019
Project MND. Additionally, proposed uses would be consistent with the current land use
designations. The current site conditions remain consistent with what was analyzed in the
previously prepared 2019 Project MND. With the proposed phasing of the TTM,
construction of the Proposed Project would occur in three phases instead of on phase as
previously proposed. Phasing the Proposed Project would add approximately two to four
months to the construction timeline; however, this extension would not be significant
enough to result in increased or new environmental effects nor is the length of
construction an environmental impact.

Based on the updated guidelines provided by CDFW regarding the western Joshua tree,
the Proposed Project would result in take of a recently listed candidate species under
CESA, the western Joshua tree. Compliance with the CDFW guidelines would not result
in substantial changes for the Proposed Project and would not require major revisions as
this information was not previously known during the preparation of the 2019 Project
 MND. Furthermore, attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and payment of CDFW
mitigation fees would ensure a less than significant impact to western Joshua tree in
addition to complying with the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance. The biological
impacts remain consistent with what was analyzed in 2019 and the Proposed Project
would not result in new or significant impacts. No new impacts would be introduced by
the Proposed Project that require major revision to the 2019 Project MND.

Condition 2:

  ▪  Substantial changes occur with respect to the circumstances under which the
  project is undertaken which will require major revisions of the previous EIR or
  Negative Declaration due to the involvement of new significant environmental
  effects or a substantial increase in the severity of previously identified significant
  effects;

Although the Proposed Project would result in take of a recently listed candidate species
under CESA, the western Joshua tree, attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and
payment of CDFW mitigation fees does not require major revisions to the 2019 Project
MND as it does not introduce new impacts or increase the severity of previously identified
effects. Attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and payment of CDFW mitigation fees
would ensure a less than significant impact to western Joshua tree in addition to
complying with the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance. Therefore, the biological
impacts remain consistent with what was analyzed in 2019.

Phasing the Proposed Project would add approximately two to four months to the
construction timeline; however, this extension would not be significant enough to result in
increased or new environmental effects. Moreover, the Proposed Project would maintain
the same site plan development footprint as the 2019 Project, and conditions on the
Project site have not changed significantly. The proposed uses will also be the same as
what was previously analyzed, including the land use designations.

The Proposed Project will not require major revisions due to the involvement of new
significant environmental effects, or a substantial increase in the severity or previously
identified effects.

Condition 3

  ▪  New information of substantial importance, which was not known and could have
  not been known that shows a project will have one or more significant effects not
  discussed in the previous Initial Study; significant effects previously examined will
  be more severe; mitigation measures found not to be feasible will be feasible and
  substantially reduce significant effects; mitigation measures are considerably
  different from those analyzed in the previous Initial Study but the Applicant declines
  to adopt the measure.

New information, which was not known and could have not been known, has been brought
 to light following approval of the 2019 Project: the western Joshua tree was listed as a
candidate species under CESA. However, as described in the Biological Letter (Appendix
A), the listing of the western Joshua tree will not result in any significant effects not
previously discussed in the Initial Study with attainment of an Incidental Take Permit and
payment of CDFW mitigation fees. Furthermore, compliance with the CDFW guidelines
and the City’s existing Joshua tree ordinance ensures a less than significant impact to
western Joshua tree.

The Proposed Project proposes the construction to occur in phases. The additional two
to four months would not result in new significant effects. There is no other new
information of substantial importance because the vacant 20.55-acre parcel was
previously analyzed for the development of a mixed-use facility with the same site plan
and development footprint as the Proposed Project. Existing conditions have not changed
significantly from that previous analysis. As previously discussed, 32 western Joshua
trees are located on the Project site, some of which will be transplanted. The proposed
uses will also be the same as what was previously analyzed, including the land use
designations. The Proposed Project will not result in more significant impacts and
mitigation measures remain feasible, adoptable, and will reduce any impacts to less than
significant.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant is requesting to construct a four-story, approximately 56,000 square foot
hotel consisting of 107 rooms and a drive through coffee shop totaling 2,500 square feet
located on a vacant parcel totaling 2.32 acres located south of West Avenue P-4 and west
of 5th Street West within the SP. The proposed development will also include full site
improvements including landscaping, lighting, parking and an outdoor pool and dining
terrace. The proposed hotel use and drive through coffee shop are allowed in the PD
(Planned Development) designation within the SP subject to review and approval of a
SPR application. In addition, as described within SP Section III.B.4., review and approval
of a CUP application is also required for requests for building height above 45 feet.

The applicant is also requesting the approval of a Type 70 (On-Sale General – Restrictive
Use) Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) license to sell or furnish beer, wine
and distilled spirits for consumption on the premise to guests of the hotel.

BACKGROUND

The project site is regulated by the SP which was originally adopted on May 24, 1990
(Resolution No. 90-152), and last amended July 11, 2017 (Ordinance No. 1498) as a
means of managing the use of land, establishing provisions for detailed site development,
providing a comprehensive approach to infrastructure planning and financing, and
providing guidance for future development and redevelopment activities in the area.

Through the recent adoption of Palmdale 2045, a comprehensive General Plan Update,
the land use designation of this site has been changed from SP (Palmdale Trade and
Commerce Center Specific Plan) to RC (Regional Commercial). Although the SP has
been rescinded with the General Plan Update, the project is consistent with the intent of
the RC designation and a complete application was submitted prior to the
October 22, 2022, effective date of Palmdale 2045. Therefore, this project will be
evaluated based on the standards and policies of the prior General Plan and SP.

The subject application was submitted on May 11, 2022, and after resolution of
completeness items, the project was deemed complete on September 14, 2022, and
scheduled for the November 10, 2022, Planning Commission meeting.

Access/Circulation

Access to the site will be provided through a single driveway on 5th Street West, which
provides access to the drive through coffee shop as well as creates a loop configuration
around the hotel with the main entrance proposed on the south façade. In addition, an
Americans with Disabilities Act path of travel will connect the sidewalk along 5th Street
West to the coffee shop and the hotel entrance and throughout the parking area to
accommodate safe pedestrian flow. Furthermore, the City Engineer reviewed the project
and determined that it is designed with adequate access to accommodate safe vehicular
flow.

Elevations

The proposed hotel and drive through coffee shop will include a variety of building
materials, colors, and textures, including, stucco, brick and metal paneling. In addition,
the varying colors of gray and brown and architectural enhancements such as varying
roof lines, canopies and building projections will be included on all sides of the building.
The varying roof lines and parapet ensure that all roof mounted equipment will be
adequately screened from public view.

Use

The proposed four-story hotel and the coffee shop will be located on an approximately
two-acre site and both uses are permitted within the PD designation of the SP subject to
review and approval of a SPR application. The hotel also requires the approval of a CUP
because the proposed maximum height of 52 feet is greater than the maximum height of
45 feet allowed within the PD designation. The increase in height for this project will
provide more guestrooms, which will bring more revenue to the City and is consistent with
the height of the existing hotel to the north, which is 84 feet tall. The proposed hotel use
will contain 107 rooms, an indoor fitness area, guest laundry facilities, an outdoor pool
and seating area and a lounge and café area, which includes a bar that proposes to
operate daily from 4:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. In addition, each guest room will be furnished
with a mini bar. As such, the applicant is also requesting approval of a Type 70 (On-Sale
General – Restrictive Service) ABC license to sell or furnish beer, wine and distilled spirits
for consumption on the premise to guests of the hotel. The hotel qualifies as an Incidental
Alcohol Beverage establishment because less than 10% of the gross floor area will be
utilized for the sale, display and storage of alcohol as shown in Table 4 and Figure 6.

SPECIAL FINDINGS FOR ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE ESTABLISHMENTS

In addition to the standard CUP findings required in PMC Section 17.22.050, the
Planning Commission must also find that the proposed use is consistent with the purpose
of PMC Section 17.92.070. That section provides:

  “It is the purpose of these regulations to establish specific standards for alcoholic
  beverage establishments to ensure that such businesses are appropriately located
  and operated so as not to pose a significant threat to the public health, safety, peace
  and welfare.”

Items that the Planning Commission may consider in making this finding include Over
Intensification, High Crime Area, Surrounding Area, and Hours of Operation. These
factors are detailed below.

Over Intensification

PMC Section 17.92.070 provides two methods to determine Over Intensification:
Population Density Method and Retail Density Method; both are discussed below.

Retail Density Method

  Over Intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments shall occur
  where the number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a radius
  of 2,500 feet of any location in question exceeds the average of the numbers of
  On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a radius of 2,500 feet of a
  sample of 20 On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments drawn at random from
  the City’s commercially zoned areas.

The Retail Density Method reveals that the project site is located within an area of the city
that experiences an over intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments.
This outcome is a result of comparing the number of active On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments, within a 2,500-foot radius of the proposed hotel, with the average number
of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a 2,500-foot radius of 20 randomly
selected On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments located within commercial areas of
the City of Palmdale.

The list of 20 randomly selected On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments and the
corresponding number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments that exist within a
2,500-foot radius of each location are indicated in Table 6. Figure 8 shows the location
of these establishments with the 2,500-foot radius indicated in red and the subject site’s
radius is shown in blue. The total number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments
within a 2,500-foot radius of the randomly selected establishments is 273 (Table 6). The
average number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a 2,500-foot radius
of a randomly selected establishment is determined by dividing the 273 total On-Sale
Alcoholic Beverage Establishments by the 20 selected establishments (273 / 20 = 14).
This calculation determines that the average number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments located within a 2,500-foot buffer of another On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
Establishment is 14.  As there are 22 existing On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments within the 2,500-foot radius of the proposed hotel, this is considered an
over intensification according to the Retail Density Method; however, as the SP is
intended to create a concentration of commercial uses, the proposed location is
appropriate and is consistent with the purpose of PMC Section 17.92.070.

High Crime Area

A high crime area is defined by PMC Section 17.16.080, as an area having a crime rate
of 120 percent or more of the average of the reporting districts within the City. According
to the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, there are 33 Crime Reporting Districts
(CRD) within the City of Palmdale, with a total of 7,502 Part I and Part II Crimes reported
for the year 2021. The average number of combined Part I and Part II Crime offenses for
the reporting period, for all 33 districts, was 227 (7,502 Part I and Part II Crimes/ 33 CRD),
and 20 percent greater than that average is 272 (227 x 1.20). The project is within CRD
2619 (Figure 9), which had a total of 688 Part I and Part II offenses, according to data
provided by the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department. Therefore, the proposed use
is within a crime reporting area that exhibits a crime rate that is 303 percent
[(688 / 227) x 100] of the Citywide average. As such, the project site is within an area
that exhibits a crime rate that is 303 percent higher compared to all crime reporting
districts across the City.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided the most current location and
date information for Part I and Part II crimes reported for 2021. As shown on the
City of Palmdale CRD 2619 Crimes map (Figure 9), the crimes are scattered throughout
the reporting district.
