Calls for Service

There have been no calls for service for the subject site because the project site is
currently vacant. However, as specified within the draft Conditions of Approval, if the
proposed business generates an increase in the number of calls for service, the Los
Angeles County Sheriff’s Department may request subsequent review of the CUP by the
Planning Commission.

Surrounding Area

As specified within PMC Section 17.92.070.D, certain separations from alcohol uses to
sensitive uses are required, which are intended to ensure that such businesses are
located in a manner that avoids significant threats to public peace, health, safety, and
welfare. The project complies with all location standards because incidental on-sale
alcoholic beverage establishments within the SP are not subject to distance separation
requirements from sensitive or similar uses. There are no sensitive noise receptors in the
surrounding area because the uses in the vicinity consist of commercial retail businesses,
restaurants, service uses, and other supportive uses. As such, the location is appropriate
for this type of use.

Operations

The bar within the hotel proposes to operate from 4:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m. daily. The
applicant will be required to comply with all Conditions of Approval, restrictions of the ABC
license, ABC regulations, and reapply for a new ABC license should the use of the
premises qualify for a different license type. The sale, storage, and display of beer, wine
and distilled spirits will utilize approximately five percent of the floor area and is incidental
to the primary use of the building as a hotel. Also, Conditions of Approval have been
included within the draft Resolution to ensure avoidance of nuisances, such as requiring
the removal of litter on a daily basis. Therefore, the proposed project is not expected to
adversely affect nearby property.

An Environmental Impact Report (EIR) was prepared in conjunction with SP approval and
on May 24, 1990 (Resolution No. CC 90-142), the City Council certified EIR 90-1 (SCH
No. 89090618). The proposed project does not include any revisions to land use
designations, permitted uses, or standards of development as envisioned by the SP. In
addition, the applicant has submitted updated studies for the project site, which have

  i.  Whether the proposed establishment would result in an Over
  Intensification of alcoholic beverage establishments.

  Based on the PMC definition of over intensification, as
  determined by the Population Density and Retail Density
  Methods, the project site is located in an area that
  experiences an over intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic
  Beverage Establishments.

  According to the Population Density Method, Over
  Intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments
  occurs where the ratio of the resident population to the
  permitted On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments (as
  defined by the California Department of Alcoholic Beverage
  Control) within the census tract exceeds the ratio of
  population to On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments for
  the City. Using this method, there is currently an over
  intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments
  because there is one On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
  Establishment for every 177 people in Census Tract 9102.18

  and one for every 1,695 people citywide. With the proposed
  On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishment there will be 101
  On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within the City
  and 26 within the subject Census Tract. This amounts to one
  establishment for every 170 people within Census Tract
  9102.18 and one for every 1,678 people citywide.

  According to the Retail Density Method, Over Intensification
  of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments shall occur
  where the number of On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
  Establishments within a radius of 2,500 feet of any proposed
  location exceeds the average of the numbers of On-Sale
  Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a radius of 2,500
  feet of a sample of 20 Other Alcoholic Beverage
  Establishments drawn at random from the City’s commercially
  zoned areas. Based on this method, the project vicinity
  experiences an over intensification of On-Sale Alcoholic
  Beverage Establishments because there are an average of 14
  On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments located within a
  2,500-foot radius of the 20 randomly selected On-Sale
  Alcoholic Beverage Establishments and 22 located within a
  2,500-foot radius of the proposed location.

  Although this area does experience an over intensification of
  On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments, the sale of
